chunks: Three narrators - Muhammad ibn Hammam said: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him saying:

Al-Qa'im will face in his war what the Messenger of Allah did not face. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah came to them while they were worshipping hollowed stones and carved wood, but the people of al-Qa'im will come out against him, interpreting the Book of Allah against him, and fighting him on the basis of it.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: How does the opposition to the Mahdi differ from the opposition to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the eschatological uniqueness of the Mahdi’s struggle, where his opponents weaponize the Quran through *ta'wil* (interpretation) rather than rejecting it outright as the Prophet did with idolaters. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Mahdi’s role in restoring the true, esoteric meaning of the Quran against those who distort it for political or sectarian gain. The comparison highlights a shift from external idolatry to internal hermeneutical conflict.
